reference: Contract cases use Bash's documented type/help builtins and the public bashtermraw help text in loadables/bashtermraw.c. There is no GNU bashtermraw command for same-script parity. For deferred PTY cases, GNU stty provides independent termios and window-size observations; terminal control bytes are checked against the documented ANSI/DEC protocol sequences.
coverage: Bash registers bashtermraw as an enabled builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented subcommand descriptions and terminal I/O contract.
Bash short help exposes the complete advertised subcommand synopsis.
Deferred PTY behavior covers termios transitions, state serialization, key decoding, terminal output, and reset recovery.
exclusions: No matching GNU bashtermraw executable exists, so no fake GNU parity cases are included.
The supplied runner closes stdin and does not provide a controlling PTY or PTY driver; terminal operations are not invoked in this suite.
Interactive timing, terminal emulator rendering, signal-driven resize handling, and hardware-specific terminal behavior remain outside this run.

cases.purpose: Verify through Bash's documented type builtin that the candidate registers bashtermraw as a shell builtin.
Check that Bash help includes representative documented behavior for raw mode, size reporting, key decoding, bracketed paste, and terminal output routing.
cases.script:
h=$(help bashtermraw)
contains() { case "$h" in *"$1"*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
contains 'Subcommands:' || exit 1
contains 'raw                save current termios + switch to raw mode' || exit 1
contains 'size               echo "ROWS COLS" (TIOCGWINSZ)' || exit 1
contains 'keypress           read one key, echo decoded name on stdout' || exit 1
contains 'PASTE-START / PASTE-END for bracketed paste' || exit 1
contains 'Terminal I/O goes to /dev/tty (or stdin if /dev/tty is unavailable)' || exit 1
printf 'documented terminal API present\n'

cases.purpose: Verify that Bash short help exposes the complete documented command synopsis, including state restore, cursor, clearing, cursor visibility, and paste controls.
cases.script:
s=$(help -s bashtermraw)
case "$s" in *'bashtermraw raw|cooked|size|stty-g|stty-set STATE|keypress|cup ROW COL|clr-eol|clr-screen|clear|reset|show [on|off]|paste on|off'*) printf 'complete synopsis present\n' ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

cases.purpose: Compare raw-mode flag changes and cooked restoration against an independently captured PTY baseline.
Exercise TIOCGWINSZ reporting and stty-g/stty-set round-trip of termios flags, control characters, speeds, and window dimensions.
Check keypress decoding for plain ASCII, control keys, CSI and SS3 navigation/function keys, modifiers, bracketed-paste boundaries, and isolated ESC timing.
Capture terminal-side output for cursor positioning, line/screen clearing, clear options, cursor visibility, and bracketed-paste toggles, including stdout redirection behavior.
Verify reset's recovery escape sequence and canonical termios restoration after controlled PTY state changes.
